Representing the Reds on derby day... 📋❤️‍🔥COME ON UNITED! 🗣️🗣️🗣️

They are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

There will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. A crackdown has led to 685 supporters being stripped of their season tickets and another 464 being sanctioned. Fans will unfurl a giant banner reading “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace” aimed at the club’s hierarchy this afternoon. You can read more here from James Ducker.

Kostoulas has given Brighton the lead away at Coventry, who are still to pick up their first Premier League point. Around five minutes until half-time in that one. It was quite some finish.

"What an outstanding finish, absolutely brilliant!"Charalampos Kostoulas fires Brighton in front with a wonderful finish 💥 pic.twitter.com/bMKJACr2bd

Both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very important in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

It has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. #1587. Jeff Ekhator back in Juventus group training after injury nightmare

Jeff Ekhator has finally rejoined his Juventus teammates on the training pitch. The young striker, signed from Genoa in the summer, took part in a full group session at the Continassa on Friday for the first time since a run of muscle problems that has so far kept him out of every competitive game in black and white.

His return gives Luciano Spalletti one more name to consider in a week when the squad has been kept together at the training centre ahead of Sunday’s visit of Napoli.

Juventus announced the permanent deal on 1 July, and Football Italia put the fee at €16m plus add ons. The 19 year old has barely been available since.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, who credits Sky Sport Italia with the news, his troubles began in the very first friendly of pre-season against Basel. He recovered in time to be named in the squad for the second Serie A round against Parma, where he stayed on the bench, but broke down again a few days later and has spent roughly two further months on the sidelines.

Di Marzio describes the forward as fully recovered, and Friday’s session with the rest of the group was his first since that setback.

Jeff Ekhator signs for Juventus from Genoa on a permanent deal! ⚪️⚫️ Welcome to the club, Jeff! 🙌

Nobody should expect Ekhator to be rushed into the starting eleven after so long without match practice. Football Italia sees him more as an extra option from the bench, giving Spalletti a third centre forward alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani.

That alone matters for a side that has struggled for goals. Juventus have scored 11 times in nine league games, and the 2-0 defeat at Genoa on Wednesday, covered in our report on Spalletti’s apology, left them level on 14 points with Napoli.

The timing of his comeback is notable. After the Genoa loss, chief executive Giovanni Carnevali met the players and the coach, and Spalletti then decided to keep the squad together at the training ground until kick off, as explained in our piece on the Juventus retreat.

Napoli come to the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November for Matchday 10, with kick off at 20:45 local time. According to the club’s own match notes, it is the first time since April 2021 that the two sides meet on the same number of points in Serie A.

Whether Ekhator makes the matchday squad will become clear when Spalletti names his group. Either way, having a fit young striker back in training is a rare piece of good news for Juventus this week.

Sources: Gianluca Di Marzio, Football Italia, Juventus

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

Manchester United share interest in AC Milan defender Koni De Winter with Liverpool and Chelsea, the newest report has claimed.

The Red Devils are preparing for the return of Premier League football, with Mauricio Pochettino set to take charge of his first game on November 22 against Liverpool.

There are concerns that his weak defence could cost the new head coach at Anfield, with the likes of Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez having struggled this season.

Pochettino is known to use an aggressive system, with the 54-year-old often asking defenders to step forward and press from the halfway line.

De Winter possesses immense speed, and the 24-year-old is far more mobile then any of United's current options at the back.

Mauricio Pochettino is the bookies' leading candidate to replace under-fire Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach should the latter get sacked.

Scrutiny on his role has intensified with the Red Devils now in the relegation zone despite salvaging a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino is currently in charge of the US national team, but his contract includes a £7million release clause. However, it is yet to be determined the true value of prising Pochettino out as that figure doesn't include buying out his backroom staff.

It is also believed within Pochettino's deal that there is another clause which would allow him to leave his US role for particular high-profile jobs, such as at Old Trafford.

Mauricio Pochettino is the bookmakers' favourite to become the next Man United head coach

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick is expected to get the sack after a poor start

#1584. Japan vs Paraguay - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 16 Nov 2026 00:29, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 03:27

Japan and Paraguay will conclude their respective 2026 schedules when they face off in Tuesday's friendly in Singapore.

The Samurai Blue pulled off a thrilling win over Brazil last time out, while Paraguay cruised to a commanding victory over Singapore in their most recent outing.

Japan head into Tuesday's fixture in fine form, having lost just one of their previous 16 internationals.

Their only defeat in that period came in the Round of 32 tie against Brazil at the 2026 World Cup, which saw them spurn a leading position in a narrow 2-1 defeat.

After conceding a late winner in that contest, Hajime Moriyasu's side managed to exact an element of revenge with a stoppage-time winner of their own in Saturday's friendly against Brazil.

The Samurai Blue looked to have wasted another strong position after Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura saw their efforts cancelled out by a Vinicius Junior brace, before Coventry City's Tatsuhiro Sakamoto turned the game back in Japan's favour with a 91st-minute goal.

Sakamoto's effort made it two wins in Japan's last three head-to-head meetings with Brazil, while making it five games without defeat since their World Cup elimination.

Japan should fancy their chances of extending their unbeaten run with a win, having won four of their previous five meetings with Paraguay (D1) since losing on penalties in the last 16 of the 2010 World Cup.

After eventually being eliminated in the quarter-finals in 2010, Paraguay had to wait 16 years until their next appearance in football's biggest tournament.

La Albirroja certainly made an impact at the 2026 World Cup, advancing to the knockout rounds before eliminating Germany on penalties in the Round of 32.

However, their run ultimately came to an end in a feisty last-16 clash against France, with Kylian Mbappe's 70th-minute penalty proving decisive as Paraguay fell to a narrow 1-0 loss.

Gustavo Alfaro's side have since made a positive return to action with three consecutive wins against Bolivia, Colombia and Singapore.

Gustavo Caballero netted a brace as Paraguay cruised to a 4-1 success in their most recent outing against Singapore, representing just the third time La Albirroja have scored two or more goals in 2026.

Their strength has ultimately been at the opposite end of the pitch, having conceded more than one goal in just two of their 11 games in the current calendar year.

Japan have announced that Daichi Kamada has been allowed to return to Crystal Palace after playing 72 minutes in the win over Brazil.

Ko Itakura, Yukinari Sugawara and Kaishu Sano are among those who could start if Moriyasu opts to rotate his side.

Sakamoto, Takumi Minamino and Koki Ogawa could come in to freshen up Japan's attack for Tuesday's friendly.

As for Paraguay, Alfaro is expected to make wholesale changes after naming an experimental XI for the win over Singapore.

Juan Jose Caceres, Gustavo Gomez and Omar Alderete are likely to come into the back four for Paraguay's final outing of 2026.

Diego Gomez, Miguel Almiron and Julio Enciso are also among those who are expected to start against Japan.

Suzuki; Sugawara, Seko, Itakura, Ito; Ka Sano, Tanaka; Sakamoto, Minamino, Nakamura; Ogawa

Gill, Caceres, G. Gomez, Alderete, Maidana; Cuenca, Galarza, D. Gomez, Almiron; Benitez, Enciso

Japan will be full of confidence after pulling off a notable win over Brazil, and while we think they will claim another victory on Tuesday, we believe the scoreline will be close against a Paraguay team that is usually a tough side to break down.

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday with both sides on 14 points and both short of key figures. Spalletti is missing seven players, while Napoli lose their suspended coach and their midfield organiser Lobotka.

Juventus and Napoli go into Sunday’s Serie A Matchday 10 meeting at the Allianz Stadium level on points. Both benches will look different. Napoli will be without their head coach, with assistant Landucci on the bench. Spalletti is still missing seven players.

Allegri was sent off in Napoli’s 3-3 home draw with Roma. Serie A’s sporting judge then punished him for disrespectful remarks to the match officials. The ban covered the trip to Monza on 28 October and now the visit to Juventus. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri dropped it, saying he feared the ban could rise to four matches. The suspension is now final.

Napoli also lost Lobotka at Monza. He was stretchered off just after the 15th minute following a challenge with Mangas. The club’s medical update found damage to the tibiofibular syndesmosis in his left ankle, without instability. He also has a low-grade injury to the anterior talofibular ligament. He has started rehabilitation, with Napoli aiming for a return against Fiorentina in the Coppa Italia on 16 December. Badiashile and Neres are also injured.

The Juventus list is longer. Yildiz is expected back in early December after a foot operation, Sky Sport Italia reported. Thuram, who had knee surgery, is due back in early 2027. Locatelli is out until 2027 after a lateral meniscus operation. Grabara, with a right-knee ACL injury, is effectively out for the season.

Nico González (right soleus), Çelik (left hamstring) and Conceição (shoulder dislocation) are all expected back after the international break. There is one return. Young forward Ekhator is available again.

Juventus arrive after an uneven run. Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus on 18 October. Spalletti’s side then won at Lecce on 25 October, with goals from McKennie and Douglas Luiz. Genoa won the next game through first-half goals from Ehizibue and Baldanzi. Koopmeiners hit the crossbar in stoppage time.

After the Genoa defeat, chief executive Carnevali held a long meeting with the squad. He told them to change course straight away, especially in their mentality. Spalletti then announced the squad would stay together from Friday evening until the Napoli game. The club wants the response to come from the players on the pitch rather than from a change of coach. John Elkann still backs Spalletti, and the coach has no intention of giving up, according to Tuttosport.

#1581. Liberia vs Cape Verde - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 16 Nov 2026 00:32

Bottom-placed Liberia host Cape Verde in a Group K fixture of 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying at the Samuel Kanyon Doe Sports Complex in Monrovia on Tuesday.

The first leg in Praia on November 13 finished 4-2 to Cape Verde, which lifted the Blue Sharks to three points in third place in a group where only the top two qualify, left Liberia on zero, and kept Mali on nine points and Rwanda on six above them.

The Lone Stars sit bottom of Group K with no points from three matches, having scored three goals and conceded eight, a goal difference of -5 that leaves them six points behind second-placed Rwanda with nine still available.

Mohammed Adil Erradi, the Belgian-Moroccan appointed on a three-year contract on May 18, has yet to win a competitive match as Liberia coach, and a group calling itself the Concerned Stakeholders for Liberian Football Development demanded his dismissal on October 9, according to the Liberian Observer, citing a salary budgeted at US$98,450 a year.

The campaign opened with a 3-1 defeat in Kigali on September 25, where Sylvanus Nimely scored the only Liberian goal, and four days later Mali won 1-0 at this ground through Martial Tia’s 79th-minute strike after goalkeeper Tommy Songo pulled out of the starting line-up during the warm-up.

In Praia on November 13 Liberia trailed 3-1 after 43 minutes, with Franklin Nyenetue’s 36th-minute equaliser cancelled out two minutes later by a corner-kick header from Dje Tavares, before Ayouba Kosiah converted a stoppage-time penalty to set the final score at 4-2.

Liberia’s back three of Jamal Arago, Sampson Dweh and Emmanuel Fully conceded to a scramble in their own box, a corner and a marking lapse in the first leg, and the defence has now shipped eight goals in three qualifiers, an average of 2.67 per match.

The head-to-head record leans away from the hosts, as Liberia have lost their last three meetings with Cape Verde (2-1 in Accra on October 7, 2021, 1-0 in Mindelo on October 10, 2021, and 4-2 on November 13), although both of their wins in the series came in Monrovia, 3-0 in July 2000 and 1-0 on June 5, 2011.

A post shared by Liberia Men's National Teams (@lbr_lonestar)

Cape Verde arrive third in Group K on three points with a goal difference of -1 (six scored, seven conceded), and a win in Monrovia would take them to six, level with the total currently held by second-placed Rwanda, who host Mali in Kigali at the same 7pm GMT kick-off.

The Blue Sharks drew all three of their World Cup group matches in June (0-0 against Spain, 2-2 against Uruguay and 0-0 against Saudi Arabia) to reach the Round of 32 on their tournament debut, where Argentina beat them 3-2 after extra time on July 3, a 111th-minute own goal from Diney Borges settling it after Deroy Duarte and Sidny Lopes Cabral had pulled Cape Verde level twice.

Bubista then left to coach Moroccan club RS Berkane, and Humberto Bettencourt, his assistant for six years, was promoted on August 19, with his first two qualifiers producing a 3-1 defeat at Mali on September 25 and a 2-1 home defeat to Rwanda on September 29.

Those results extended a winless run to six matches, counting the World Cup (three draws and three defeats), which ended in Praia when Ayoni Santos, Dje Tavares, Dailon Livramento and substitute Derensili Sanches Fernandes scored in the 4-2 win, Bettencourt’s first victory in charge.

Cape Verde have conceded in all three of their qualifiers, seven goals at 2.33 per match, compared with five conceded across four World Cup matches, two of which were clean sheets against Spain and Saudi Arabia.

Bettencourt brought in six players for the double-header, among them David Moreira, Yuran Fernandes, Leandro Andrade, Ieltsin Camoes and Sanches Fernandes, and three of the four scorers in Praia (Santos, Tavares and Sanches Fernandes) were finding the net for the senior side for the first time.

Liberia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Cape Verde Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Liberia captain Oscar Dorley, the Al-Taawoun midfielder, is out with a hamstring injury and was left out of Erradi’s 24-man squad, while goalkeeper Derrick Julu of Niger Tornadoes was recalled to replace Songo, who has not featured since withdrawing from the Mali line-up on September 29.

Julu replaced Ashley Williams at half time in Praia, and Erradi said afterwards that Williams, who had played well against Mali, was not at his best, which points to Julu starting in goal on Tuesday.

Nyenetue, who plays for Ranheim, scored the equaliser in Praia and was replaced by William Gibson after 64 minutes with no injury reported.

Without Dorley, Nohan Kenneh and Solomon Tweh are the likeliest holding pairing in a four-man midfield that also used Edward Ledlum and Divine Teah of Slavia Prague, with Sampson Dweh of Viktoria Plzen anchoring the back three.

For the visitors, defender Wagner Pina, who had joined the training camp in Portugal, did not travel to Cape Verde for the first leg, and Bettencourt wished him a quick recovery.

The 26-man squad named on November 4 includes Vozinha, 40, defenders Logan Costa and Lopes Cabral, midfielder Jamiro Monteiro and 36-year-old captain Ryan Mendes, although Lopes Cabral was replaced at half time in Praia by Steven Moreira and the reason has not been given.

Bettencourt could keep the 4-1-4-1 that scored four in Praia, with Deroy Duarte shielding the back four, and he used all five substitutions there (Moreira, Monteiro, Laros Duarte, Sanches Fernandes and Camoes), which leaves a bench that is already familiar with the plan.

Julu; Fully, Dweh, Jamal, Nimely; Ledlum, Tweh, Kenneh, Nyenetue; Teah, Kosiah

Vozinha; J. Paulo, Diney, Costa, L. Cabral; D. Duarte; Mendes, Tavares, Santos, Varela; Livramento

The first leg showed where this tie will be decided, as Liberia conceded to a scramble in their own box, a corner and a marking lapse inside 43 minutes, and with Dorley absent and Erradi having already changed goalkeepers at half time, he has fewer ways to repair that in four days than Bettencourt has to exploit it again.

Liberia deserve credit for scoring twice in Praia and for restricting Mali to a 79th-minute winner on the synthetic surface at this ground, and both of their wins over Cape Verde came in Monrovia, but the later of them is 15 years old and Cape Verde’s own record of conceding in every qualifier gives the hosts a route to one goal, which is why 1-2 is a better call than a repeat of the four-goal margin.

A Cape Verde win would lift them to six points, which only equals Rwanda’s tally if the Amavubi lose to Mali in Kigali on the same evening, so Bettencourt’s side cannot treat the second leg as a formality.

#1580. HMRC chase the estate of late ex-England manager Sven-Goran Eriksson for £3.5MILLION in unpaid tax - because he was 'too busy with his ladies to save'

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:19 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 06:25 EST, 10 November 2026

Sven-Goran Eriksson's estate is being chased by HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) for an outstanding £3.5million in tax owed.

It comes as a result of the estate's inheritance following Eriksson's death in August 2024 due to pancreatic cancer.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport last year, the former England manager reportedly had assets worth £4.8m but owed a staggering £7.25m to HMRC alone. He also reportedly had at least £1m outstanding in other debts.

In a bid to help reduce that outstanding debt, his family sold his old mansion called Bjorkefors last year - albeit at a substantial loss.

Eriksson is survived by his son Johan, 47, and daughter Lina, 39 - from his first marriage to Ann-Christine Pettersson - as well as partner Yaniseth Alcides. During his time as England manager he had a high-profile relationship with Nancy Dell'Olio.

Speaking to The Sun, Eriksson's lawyer Anders Runebjer has revealed that the estate has no money left to settle the debt - aside from £300,000 in a UK bank and £1m in a Cayman Islands tax haven. He also stated his focus is now to salvage any money for Eriksson's two children after the ex-Three Lions boss had spent his finances around football and women.

Ex-England manager Sven-Goran Eriksson's estate is being chased for £3.5million by HMRC

In August 2024, he passed away at the age of 76 following a battle with pancreatic cancer

The Swede is survived by his two children Johan, 47, and daughter Lina, 39

'Sven earned millions but was always too busy with his football and his ladies to manage money very well,' said Runebjer.

'I told the HMRC I'm not able to get the money in the Cayman Islands or his UK bank and said they're welcome to seize it.

'They replied that they couldn't do that so I told them there was nothing else left - so they won't get paid.

'Sven was regularly sent bills by the British taxman and paid promptly but they changed the rules and now say he still owes £3.5m plus interest after he passed away.

'They're welcome to take whatever they can get but I'm not giving them anything.

'My priority is trying to get whatever money I can that he left for his children - not the British taxman.'

As aforementioned, Eriksson's estate sold his seven-bed house in Torsby, in his native Sweden - located on the banks of Lake Fryken - but at a reduced price.

According to The Sun, the property was on the market for £2m but his family had to lower the price by £400,000 to attract any prospective buyers.

And they went on to add that an anonymous e-commerce businesswoman has now bought it for an undisclosed sum of at least £1.3m - meaning a potential £700,000 loss on market value alone. However, the loss is greater as Eriksson bought the place in 2002 for £4.5m - meaning the true value lost is around £3m.

Last year, Eriksson's former home in Sweden was sold as his family look to reduce debt

Eriksson lived in the property with his partner Yaniseth Alcides until his death

During his time as England boss, he was in a high-profile relationship with Nancy Dell'Olio

Selling the property was the latest thing Eriksson's family have done in a bid to ease the financial burden they have taken on since his death.

In March 2025, they were forced to auction off his memorabilia - such as a lunch invitation from the late Queen.

Also up for auction was his Armani suit from a 2006 World Cup match with his hand-written team notes still in the pocket.

The 349 items reported to have gone under the hammer for a combined total of £140,000 also include his BBC Coach of the Year trophy in 2001 and a Premier League Manager of the Month award from his time as Manchester City boss.

An Ivory Coast top signed with a special message by former forward Didier Drogba from Eriksson's time as national coach in 2010 was sold as well.

Eriksson was estimated to have received around £7m in pay-offs alone from England, Manchester City and Mexico during his managerial career.

The Swede, who managed England between 2001 and 2006, previously described himself as being 'stupid' with his money.

In one of his last ever interviews, he told The Guardian: 'I was never interested in money - I never took care of it and trusted people to do that for me. I was stupid not to control where the money went. I realised that when I didn't have any more cash!

'I still don't know what I have in the bank.'

#1579. Spalletti calls job question provocative and vows no step back before Napoli

Luciano Spalletti struck a defiant tone on the eve of Juventus-Napoli, a game seen as a must-win. He also backed the club's response to the defeat at Genoa, including a squad retreat.

Spalletti made his stance clear on the eve of Juventus-Napoli. Anyone expecting him to retreat even slightly, he warned, should expect something different.

Sunday’s game is at the Allianz Stadium. Spalletti said the side want to win back the respect that has been taken from them. Several outlets say his job is on the line.

The build-up has been shaped by the club’s response to the defeat at Genoa. Ehizibue scored in the 12th minute and Baldanzi in the 28th. After a long meeting between chief executive Giovanni Carnevali and the squad, Spalletti announced a retreat. The team would stay at the Continassa from Friday evening until the Napoli game.

Spalletti called Carnevali’s address perfect and said he had hit the right notes. He has never been keen on training-camp retreats. In these circumstances, though, he said one could help the group become more compact again.

The coach also played down any need for public backing. He needs no reassurance from the club, only a reaction from the team, Eurosport reported. He added that he is not asking his players for anything beyond their capabilities.

After nine rounds, this season’s tally trails the 15 Juventus had at the same stage last season and the 17 under Motta in 2024/25. It is above the 13 under Allegri in 2022/23, according to Tuttosport.

Recent form has been uneven. The last five league results were a 2-0 home win over Atalanta, a 1-1 draw at Cagliari and a 3-0 home defeat by Lazio. A 2-0 win at Lecce and the loss at Genoa complete the run. Two of those five games ended in defeat, and Juventus failed to score in both.

Napoli arrive without their coach. The Serie A sporting judge banned Massimiliano Allegri for two matches over disrespectful remarks to the officials in the 3-3 draw with Roma. The ban covers the Monza and Juventus games.

Spalletti also offered a hint on selection. He said Edon Zhegrova and Jeremie Boga would come on in the second half even if they did not start.

There is little time to recover whatever the result. Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League on Thursday 5 November at 21:00.

#1578. Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

“That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

It’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

James pounces on a loose ball, dribbles infield from the right. No one bothers to close him down so he eventually has a shot, blazing over with his left from 20 yards.

Late free-kick for Leeds after Livramento bundled Aaronson over. Wilson chips from the left to the far post and Muharemovic heads it back acros goal looking for a team-mate but none had made the run.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 1 (Touré) No clean sheet for Leeds. Farke is fuming after the substitute exploits an error and scores with a left-foot shot that deflects off Justin.

Livramento drives the ball 60 yards looking for Barnes but the ball skids off the turf and into Trafford’s arms.

Crunching Bard tackle on Bamba sends the ball to James who lets fly from 22 yards into the shins of a Newcastle defender.

Bard is penalised for a trip on Barnes as the game peters out.

Ampadu and Bamba collide when fighting for a loose ball but there was nothing malicious in it.

Wissa escapes a booking for a snide kick at Muharemovic’s shin.

A debatable offside call which should have been left for VAR lets Trafford off the hook when he comes out of his area to clear a ball clipped over the top. He slices it to Toure and the ref stops the game but I think Bard was playing Wissa, who found Toure, onside.

Newcastle corner on the left headed out by Elvedi and Barnes recovers the ball to start another attack with the 18-yard line stacked with players. When the diagonal comes back from left to right Barnes heads it behind for a goalkick.

Willock hooks a half-volley on to the roof of the net.

Bard → GudmundssonAaronson → OkaforWilson → Tanaka

Newcastle free-kick for a trip on Willock. Hall takes and Leeds head it out for a throw-in.

Livramento improves the quality of crosses with two that at least find the middle of the box even if they were headed away by Elvedi and Justin respectively.

Newcastle are enjoying more possession but the crossing has been awful when they do get down the flanks, Touré the latest offender.

Barnes shoots down Trafford’s throat. Barnes had thrown himself down in the box moments earlier and there was a VAR check but there was nothing like the contact required to send him swan-diving on to the grass.

Wissa gets down the right and whips over a low cross but Willock’s touch was too heavy.

There was a piece in the Athletic today saying Newcastle pivoted to Hornicek instead of pursuing Trafford again because he had a very high ceiling and was younger. He hasn’t caught much here, dropping the ball even when he chooses not to punch.

Matthias Jaissle promised high intensity, high octane, front foot football when he was interviewed for the Newcastle job. He and sporting director Ross Wilson have repeated that promise several times since he was appointed. There has been no sign of it since the opening weekend against Liverpool.

Newcastle are passive, they look disorganised in midfield and weak at the back. Oh and they barely apply pressure let alone attack dangerously.

These are early days but this performance and result had been coming. A pretty brutal reality check after all the positive noise and bold predictions in pre-season. This defeat will drop Newcastle to 12th in the table, where they finished last season under Eddie Howe.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 0 (Okafor) Ampadu hurls it into the box. A defender heads it to the edge of the area where Okafor thumps a left-footed half-volley in off the right post.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Livramento slides in to stop Okafor’s drive down the left, giving Leeds another opportunity to throw it long.

Triple change: Livramento → DedicTouré → Fernandez-PardoWillock → Murphy

Leeds catch Newcastle playing short from the back. Stach blindsides Steur 20 yards out, tackles him, cuts inside then bends a left foot shot into the side-netting.

After Hall stings Trafford’s palms with a strike from distance. Newcastle want a penalty when the ball hits Tanaka’s arm … but it was outside the area and then Murphy, in frustration, chops down Gudmundsson and takes the booking as an occupational hazard.

Elvedi sloppily gives the ball way to Wissa who tries to set Fernandez-Pardo through down the left. Justin sticks with him and Bogle mops up after Justin was tripped.

Gudmundsson does the upended beetle when he tries to break from the corner and collides with a Newcastle player. He claims he was fouled and wthrashes about like a RL player after he’s tackled. He continues to do a Rumpelstiltskin polka of peevishness towards the ref for a while.

Newcastle corner on the left that Trafford backpedals to tip behind for another.

No changes at half-time for Newcastle as they kick off. Leeds break through the middle quickly and Calvert-Lewin seems to push the ball past Botman and shapes to shoot before Steur slides in with a crucial tackle just inside the box.

The first goal is now an own goal. The explanation is that Tanaka’s shot was on target but the deflection from Steur meant it was going wide until it hit Miley.

Now the second goal has been credited to Bogle as Calvert-Lewin’s header struck the top of his head before it went in.

You could not say that this scoreline is undeserved. Newcastle are being demolished physically. The central midfield two – Steur and Miley – just don’t have the power to screen their defence.

Leeds 3 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Leeds are running all over Newcastle who seem physically flimsy. Calvert-Lewin chops in from the left on to a flick-on, the ball takes a deflection off the Newcastle captain and he steers it into the far corner with a right-foot shot.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

Calvert-Lewin is booked for catching Botman in the face with a straight arm rather than a swinging arm. ‘Reckless but not violent.’ Trafford had punchd the corner away at the back post to set Leeds off on a counter.

Tanaka gives the ball away carelessly in midfield and Newcastle work it to Wissa who chops inside past Elvedi, hangs out his own leg looking for contact and hits the deck. The ref waves play on and the ball runs to Barnes in the left of the area. He shapes to shoot but Muharemovic sprinted over to make a fine block-tackle, forcing it behind for a corner.

Newcastle are rocking here. They cannot win a tackle.

For those of us who have watched all Newcastle United’s games this season, this was coming. They do not have any consistent attacking threat, they do no create chances and they are not secure at the back either.

They’ve survived by converting the very few chances they create in games but they have not even had a shot in the first half here.

Leeds should be three up after Hornicek fumbled Gudmundsson’s shot from the left. The ball falls to Calvert-Lewin five yards out and he triesto dink it over the keeper who recovers well to smother it.

Leeds 2 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Newcastle try to play the ball out from the back, give it away cheaply to Bogle who feeds Justin haring down the right. He is ostensibly the right centre-back but he is a full-back by trade and stands up a perfect near-post cross that Calvert-Lewin hangs in the air to bury with the firmest of headers. In fact it transpires that his downward header struck Bogle and another deflection benefits rampant Leeds –162 seconds between the goals.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

Leeds 1 Newcastle 0 (Tanaka) Good move, spawny finish. Tanaka sprays a pass out to Okafor who drives at Dedic then picks out Tanaka who had held his run. He cushions the pass then lets fly. The ball hits Steur, deflects on to Miley and then loops into the right of the goal with Hornicek understandably stranded.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Good tackle by Steur on Bogle stops the Leeds right-back flying forward after Calvert-Lewin’s flick-on.

Newcastle really are not afraid to launch the ball forward are they? Football tactics are constantly evolving and fashions come back around. What better way to play through a press than to bypass the midfield completely? The hope is it will also cause the centre-backs problems, get them facing their own goal under pressure from one of Newcastle’s rapid forward players in a foot race.

It almost worked a couple of times in the first half but it should be pointed out that the best direct/long ball teams of the past tended to have a striker who was dominant in the air. Newcastle do not currently have one which does limit their threat from flick ons.

Newcastle break from defending a long throw. Wissa carries it 60 yards but with Murphy and Fernadez-Pardo better placed, he tries to shoot from 25 yards and plinks it straight at Trafford, provoking an inevitable ‘Woooooooo’.

From the resulting long throw Elvedi is found at the back post, unmarked and attempts to volley it towards goal, missing the ball entirely. It was so wild that even the Leeds staff laugh at how inept it was.

Leeds have a corner when they use one of their signature moves, Bogle cutting in from the right across the back four to take a ball over the top. He controls it but cannot force it past Thiaw.

Hornicek claws out the corner to Bogle 18 yards out. He puts his laces through a volley that Hornicek parries up high and punches away when he has a second go.

Newcastle chip it long again, this time down the right. Gudmundsson holds off Murphy and Leeds will have the relief of a goal-kick.

Leeds are finding it hard now to play through Newcastle’s high press and the intensity with which they are hounding keeper and defenders.

Newcastle keep looking to use their pace with balls over the top for Wissa, Murphy and Fernandez-Pardo. Wissa closes Trafford down quickly again. He needs to release it with more urgency.

Gonzalez hs not recovered from being struck on the head by the ball and is being replaced by Steur as a concussion sub.

Justin heads over his own bar when Newcastle chip a long pass down the inside right. Wissa beats Muharemovic and tries to find Fernandez-Pardo but Justin got there first. Newcastle go short from the corner and Leeds force them back into their own half.

Terrific save from Hornicek down low to his right. Tanaka’s cross from the left found Justin creeping round the back on the right and heading across goal from the back post. Bogle swivelled and tried a sidewinder flick that was arrowing towards the bottom left corner until the keeper swooped to turn it away with his right hand.

Wissa is ticking, feeling he is getting nothing from the referee when challenging for the ball, the latest incident involving a collision with Justin which was 50-50.

Leeds have been the slicker of the two sides, their passing and movement causing the full-backs problems. Okafor dribbles down the left and centres. Stach lays it back to Ampadu who hammers a half-volley from 18 yards that poleaxes Calvert-Lewin who was in an offside position.

Newcastle fans sing ‘There’s only one Kevin Keegan’ as the visitors’ defence sweeps the ball around. When they knock the ball up the inisde-right channel Wissa is penalised for swinging his arm and catching Muharemovic in the mooey.

Wissa presses Trafford high and the goalkeeper is a bit too casual but gets away with it. His clearance bounces off the attacker’s shin and loops out to the right. Leeds shift it quickly out to the left with Gudmundsson and Okafor bombing forward. A vicious cross from the left-back hits a Newcastle leg, loops up and smaxks Gonzales flush in the face, knocking him off his feet. The ref stops play.

Two bad moments for Newcastle early on. Lewis Hall caught out by a simple run and pass behind him and then, from the resulting corner Mathias Fernandez-Pardo looked very fortunate, in my opinion, to avoid conceding a penalty for handball.

He got the benefit of the doubt presumably because the ball bounced up onto his hand as he tried to bring it under control and he did not intend to control it with his hand or knock it away. The handball law confuses me but there is a higher threshold now.

Stach tackles Wissa in the centre-circle. Wissa is playing behind Fernandez-Pardo. Ampadu receives a long pass over the top, coming back from an offside position in the nick of time.

Fernandez-Pardo’s outstretched left arm is struck in the penalty area with the ball after they win the header but the ref waves play on and stops the game for a foul on the new striker.

It’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. There are problems with VAR, though, and the whole stadium has just seen the ball strike Matias Fernanzes-Pardo’s hand in the area. The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. It is preposterous that faceless beaks have distorted the game so much.

Leeds kick off, attacking the South Stand, from left to right, as they always prefer to do. Justin and Bogle combine on the right and Bogle bends a pass inside HAll to Stach who chooses to cross rather than shoot. It hits Botman and goes out for a corner.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as quickly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

The start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always important to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

The result followed a difficult run. Juventus had won just one of their previous four Serie A games. Their last outing ended in a 0-2 defeat against Genoa. Some home fans jeered the team early in the second half.

Napoli’s own match report described the first hour as balanced, with good chances for both teams, before Juventus took control. Guglielmo Vicario made an excellent early save to keep out a diving header from Lorenzo Lucca. Juan Cabal hit the post before the half-hour mark.

Spalletti changed the game from the bench. Federico Gatti replaced Weston McKennie at the break. Edon Zhegrova came on for Randal Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. The substitute skipped past Rrahmani and laid the ball off to Alajbegović. Alajbegović cut inside and fired a left-footed shot into the far corner beyond Alex Meret.

Napoli were then reduced to ten men. Kelly and Jérémie Boga had replaced Jhon Lucumí and Alajbegović on 72 minutes. Andrea Cambiaso came on for Cabal on 83. He set up Boga, who sealed the win with a right-footed curler three minutes from time.

Sky Sport Italia’s ratings made Alajbegović man of the match and called the win important for keeping Juventus in the race for the European places. Across the full 90 minutes, the match statistics favoured the home side. Juventus had 18 shots to Napoli’s 8, with 4 on target against 1. They also won 13 corners to 4. Possession was almost level, at 49% to 51%.

After ten games, Spalletti’s side have five wins, two draws and three defeats. Lazio lead the table on 28 points after nine wins and a draw.

#1576. Jordan vs Australia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 16 Nov 2026 00:33

Jordan and Australia will face off in a rare November international friendly at King Abdullah Stadium on Tuesday.

The home side are striving for consistency following their group-stage exit from the 2026 World Cup, while Australia will be looking to make it back-to-back away victories.

Jordan may have fallen short of the group-stage hurdle at their first-ever World Cup, but they still produced some memorable moments for their supporters.

Despite suffering a 3-1 defeat to Austria in their opening game, Ali Olwan's stunning strike remains fresh in the memory.

Jordan failed to win either of their remaining matches against Algeria and Argentina, but they showed no shortage of fighting spirit before their World Cup campaign came to an end.

Badou Zaki's side are now without a win in their last 10 matches and have recorded two draws since the tournament.

The Chivalrous Ones played out a 1-1 draw against Syria in their first match after the World Cup in September before being held to a goalless stalemate by Venezuela in October, extending their winless run through two underwhelming friendlies.

In contrast, Australia enjoyed a memorable tournament, reaching the knockout stages despite being drawn in a difficult group.

Tony Popovic's side stunned many with a 2-0 victory over a strong Turkey outfit in their opening match.

They subsequently lost 2-0 to the USA, but a goalless draw was enough to secure their passage into the knockout rounds, where they suffered a 4-2 penalty shootout defeat to Egypt after the match finished 1-1 in normal time.

Australia faced Brazil twice in international friendlies after the World Cup, drawing 1-1 in the first encounter before losing 4-2 in the return fixture.

However, they head into this contest with renewed confidence after thrashing Qatar 3-0 earlier this week, with all three goals arriving in the first half.

Zaki has a fully fit squad at his disposal, and it will be interesting to see which combination he opts for.

Abdallah Al-Fakhouri could retain his place in goal, although Alec Samir featured in the 1-1 draw against Syria.

World Cup hero Mousa Al-Tamari is expected to lead the attack alongside Olwan and veteran forward Mahmoud Al-Mardi.

Australia, meanwhile, are missing several key players, with Cameron Burgess ruled out by a cruciate ligament injury and Jordan Bos also sidelined with a knee problem.

In midfield, Kai Trewin and Rangers midfielder Cameron Devlin are both unavailable due to injury.

Popovic will also have to make do without Mohamed Toure and Cristian Volpato for this encounter, although the Socceroos still have enough quality in their ranks to cope with the absentees.

Jordan will be desperate to secure their first victory since 2025 and should fancy their chances against an Australian side missing several key players. However, the visitors will be keen to end the international break unbeaten, and we expect an entertaining contest to finish level.

#1574. What Man United, with their seemingly addictive habit, must do now once Michael Carrick is sacked: IAN LADYMAN on Sir Jim Ratcliffe's trail of bad judgment and waste

Published: 02:00 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 07:53 EST, 10 November 2026

Those who were there will never forget the utter chaos of Michael Carrick’s last act at Old Trafford. But as the outgoing United manager clung on to his dignity like a life raft in those mad closing moments against Aston Villa, the current poster boy for United’s desperate demise sat on the bench in his tracksuit.

Diogo Dalot is an honest and by all accounts fully committed Portuguese full-back who has been a United player for more than eight years.

The 27-year-old was bought for his teenage potential by his compatriot Jose Mourinho in 2018 but has never trained on. He has never been good enough for a really top English club yet has made more than 250 appearances for the most famous one of all and has played for five different permanent managers.

On Sunday he was booed off by his own supporters when substituted after an hour. His had been a particularly grim performance but the boos were not about him, not really.

No they were not about Dalot but instead about the fundamental truth of what he represents. Namely a steady, grisly and unforgivable drain of footballing standards at United that actually began in the final days of Sir Alex Ferguson and has subsequently never stopped.

It is this that has taken United from Ferguson’s final valedictory title of 2013 to where they are today, the bottom three of the Premier League. It is this that has drained United of all their clout and reputation. It is this that has cost yet another United manager – a seventh – his job.

Diogo Dalot has become the poster boy for the decline under Michael Carrick as Man United seemingly plumb new depths

The outgoing club legend is not a good enough manager for United and his appointment was yet another mis-step by the club's hierarchy

Carrick is not a good enough manager for United. His appointment was an emotional mistake, one of many made by Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the band of misfits and hopefuls who are currently in charge of football operations.

With a better manager – a better coach – in charge of the current team, United would be in the top half of the league. The fact they sit 18th and resemble a Sunday League team that never gets going until they have shaken their hangovers off is squarely down to him.

Nevertheless, United are a football club that exists to win trophies, no matter what the majority owners the Glazers may have said recently. But United will not win the big trophies again until they buy better players and by that I mean better footballers and better people.

It sounds simple, trite even. But it’s a simple truth of our game. Until United can reverse a seemingly addictive habit of paying too much money for too little, the difference made by a manager will only ever be a matter of six or seven places in the Premier League standings. And United needs a much greater improvement than that until this vicious cycle of self-harm comes to an end.

There is so much wrong at the modern Manchester United away from the field. Much of it begins and ends with the hideous hubris and self-regard of Ratcliffe, a man so shot through with misplaced self-confidence that he still insists on being tailed everywhere by a journalist he has hired to write a book on United’s journey back to the top of the mountain. Suffice to say that one won’t be ready for this Christmas.

But the thread that links the final days of Ferguson and his chief executive David Gill through the years of Ed Woodward, Richard Arnold and John Murtough to these dark days of Ratcliffe’s INEOS control is simple. It’s sub-standard players.

Despite the financial drain of the Glazers’ stranglehold, United have spent in the region of £1.75bn on their first team in the last ten years.

It takes quite something to do that and take a club backwards. It takes quite something to do that and buy only one player – captain Bruno Fernandes – who can claim to have been consistently effective over his time at the club.

Somehow, though, United have managed it and it is this hideous trail of bad judgment and waste that follows the current team and those that have come before it every time it runs out on to the field.

United are weak off the pitch and even weaker on it. Their football mirrors their off-field strategy. Haphazard, wasteful and inconsistent.

A number of years ago – at a time when previous CEOs Woodward and Arnold were trying to mend a broken club - they enlisted the advice of Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton and former captain Bryan Robson to help them work out what exactly a United team should be.

‘Exciting, daring, confident and humble’ were the key words they laid down. Well, what on earth happened to any of that?

United have a huge decision to make – yet again – over a new manager. The field of suitable candidates is not as big as they would like. Nor is United as attractive a proposition as it was. The demands are enormous yet the foundations shake. It’s not a good combination.

A good coach would improve them. Carrick has had two central defenders on his staff in Jonny Evans and Jonathan Woodgate. What on earth have they been doing for the last two or three months?

Long before the arrival of Jim Ratcliffe former chief executive Ed Woodward and Richard Arnold attempted to draw a blueprint for the club

Their successors in the boardroom Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have not impressed over a baffling summer

But United remain four or five good transfer windows away from where they need to be and the last time they put a run of good business like that together at Old Trafford Carrick was probably in the first team.

United need proper talent but they also need proper people, not the kind who would rather moan to TV cameras after a defeat than go home and think about their own part in what has just happened.

Last summer’s strategy seemed to have come straight out of Chat GPT and reflects terribly on the current football director Jason Wilcox. To ‘fix’ the midfield through three signings with the need to ‘fix’ the back four kicked down the road for 12 months is not so much a strategy as an exercise in transfer suicide.

Some think Wilcox should follow Carrick through the door on the back of that and it’s a reasonable point of view. Viewed through the mist of an autumn afternoon on Sunday, Wilcox looked as grey as his recent track record. An alternative take is that the recruitment of players like Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha is indicative of an uptick in returns, at least in part.

Whichever path you wish to walk, it simply has to lead to an improvement in the one area that will either nourish or starve a football club. With that in mind, the first question a prospective manager should ask is who is buying the players and on the back of what long-term strategy.

Carrick’s United team have looked like exactly what they are this season, a group put together by different people following different principles for different managers. How strange that it hasn’t worked.

United, as we know, needed a left-back over the summer. Lewis Hall, of England and Newcastle, may have been an option. Instead, United placed their faith in Luke Shaw, a 31-year-old with a long history of injuries.

Shaw, unsurprisingly, is currently injured which brings us back to where we started, namely the sight of the right-footed Dalot labouring out of position on the left of Carrick’s back four against Villa on Sunday.

You could say we saw this coming. Many did. In the dressing room and in the stands at Old Trafford. Carrick? He knew about it, too, but then he was only the manager.

His exit will hurt for a while. He is an emotionally intelligent and empathetic individual who will reel from the trauma of the last ten weeks. Over time he will realise that he is well out if it, though. When he took the job last summer, Ferguson is known to have been concerned about what it may do to him. As often, Carrick’s old boss was right.

United are set up to fail and Carrick’s replacement will realise that soon enough. When he walks into the first team dressing room for the first time and looks for those upon whom he can rely to consistently help him, too many eyes will be focussed on the floor.

Weston McKennie will miss Thursday's Europa League game at AZ Alkmaar with fatigue in his right adductor, though he has no muscle tear. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal are fit again, a relief for a badly stretched squad before a demanding trip.

Juventus will travel to AZ Alkmaar without Weston McKennie. The American has fatigue in his adductor and will sit out Thursday’s Europa League match. The news is not all bad. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal, who also came off in the 2-0 win over Napoli, have both been cleared.

#1572. Poland vs Sweden - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 01:18

Fighting for a chance at survival in UEFA Nations League B, Poland will welcome Group B4 winners Sweden to Tarczynski Arena on Tuesday.

The Eagles are under pressure, though the Blue and Yellow have already clinched top spot and could be caught off guard.

Jan Urban's Poland have endured a dire campaign so far, and the best they can hope for at this stage is to qualify for the League B/C playoffs.

The Eagles only required a draw against Romania last time out to secure a place in an inter-division showdown, but they were beaten 2-1 in Bucharest on Saturday.

That defeat has left Urban's side third in Group B4 with four points to their name, just one clear of Romania ahead of the final matchday.

Knowing that victory for their rivals could force them into the automatic relegation spot, Poland will be fearing a clash against in-form Sweden, especially after losing three of their last four outings.

However, the hosts will take heart from the fact they are unbeaten on home soil during this group stage, having drawn 0-0 with Bosnia-Herzegovina on September 25, before thrashing Romania 6-0 a week later.

Meanwhile, Graham Potter's Sweden are yet to taste defeat in Group B4, and are set to play League A football next term following an excellent campaign.

The Blue and Yellow held on to beat Bosnia-Herzegovina 3-2 on Saturday, racing into a three-goal lead courtesy of a fifth-minute opener from Borussia Dortmund's Daniel Svensson and a pair of penalties from Arsenal's Viktor Gyokeres, but conceded twice in a tense second half.

That performance fits Sweden's pattern, considering they have scored in the first 20 minutes during six of their last seven Nations League clashes, while 13 of their past 15 matches have seen both sides find the back of the net.

Regardless, securing their fourth win in five games has Potter's men top of the group with 13 points, five clear of the second-placed Dragons and nine above third-placed Poland.

The Blue and Yellow may no longer be under pressure, but they will be keen to end on a positive note, and having won eight of their last nine meetings with Poland, supporters will be looking forward to another triumph on Tuesday.

Poland will be without Porto centre-back Jakub Kiwior, who is suspended due to accumulating yellow cards, while Aston Villa right-back Matty Cash is a doubt with a leg problem and goalkeeper Kamil Grabara is sidelined with a cruciate ligament injury.

In their absence, Kacper Potulski could be joined by Tomasz Kedziora at the heart of the hosts' defence, flanked by Arkadiusz Pyrka and Oskar Kubiak at full-back in front of shot-stopper Bartlomiej Dragowski.

Elsewhere, Inter Milan midfielder Piotr Zielinski is unavailable due to illness, though Sebastian Szymanski and Wiktor Nowak should be on hand to start in the centre of the park.

By Lewis Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 01:44

Arsenal forward Christos Tzolis has avoided serious injury despite feeling discomfort after Greece's game against the Netherlands, the latest report has revealed.

The Gunners will resume their quest for the Premier League title on Saturday, when they take on Newcastle United in matchweek 11.

However, there are fears that Mikel Arteta's squad may be weakened further ahead of that clash at St James' Park.

Winger Tzolis has already suffered a hamstring injury this season, missing four league matches, but he was taken off in the 73rd minute of Greece's clash with the Netherlands on Friday.

Journalist Dimitris Manakos has revealed that the winger had an MRI scan due to discomfort, though he has not suffered a serious injury and has not been ruled out of Monday's match against Serbia.

While there is no suggestion that Tzolis will miss Saturday's game for Arsenal, it would not be surprising if he started on the bench in order to avoid an injury occurring.

The Gunners will likely start Kai Havertz as a striker, while Noni Madueke is also set to feature on the right side of attack.

Other than Tzolis, there is no natural left-winger in the squad, and that could force Arteta to select Eberechi Eze for that flank.

Tzolis has not scored for the Gunners this season, and while he has registered four assists, two came in the Community Shield.

The Greek international's performances arguably do not merit a place in the team, but Arsenal may not have a better option on the left.

Madueke can play on both flanks, though he has been forced to fill in for Bukayo Saka on the right, while Eze has consistently failed to impress out wide.

Arsenal should not be in a position where they have to rely on Tzolis, and the fact Arteta does not have an elite wide player on the left is a damning indictment of the club's transfer policy in recent years.

Juventus have tied academy forward Destiny Elimoghale to the club until 30 June 2029, on the day Giovanni Carnevali spoke to shareholders about the youth sector. The 2009-born striker has already been named in a European squad while injuries stretch the first team.

The club announced Elimoghale’s renewal on 3 November. That was the same day chief executive Giovanni Carnevali addressed shareholders at the Allianz Stadium. He called for a single project covering the first team, the Next Gen and the youth sector.

Elimoghale has come through every level of the club’s academy. He has been at Juventus since childhood. This season he began playing professional football in Serie C.

The NEC fixture was the opening matchday of the Europa League league phase. Spalletti named three Next Gen players because the first team was hit by injuries, Tuttosport reported. Pagnucco and Owusu joined Elimoghale. All three were in a European squad for the first time.

Elimoghale did not get on the pitch in the comfortable win. He stayed on the bench as an unused substitute, alongside Vicario, Pinsoglio and Pagnucco.

Back in Serie C, his minutes have been mixed. In a 5-3 home defeat to Albinoleffe on the sixth matchday, he tried two long-range shots. One went just wide. Goalkeeper Baldi saved the other. At Trento on the 11th matchday, he replaced Leone in the 70th minute of a 2-1 defeat. The match came in Serie C Group A. He was among Massimo Brambilla’s unused substitutes in the 1-1 home draw with Pro Vercelli on 2 November. That matchday 12 fixture was the Next Gen’s most recent game.

Carnevali said the club must bring its youth sector back to the level of recent years. He added that Juventus must keep trying to improve it. Securing a home-grown forward for the long term is consistent with that message.

Carnevali confirmed a change to the UEFA squad list as well, with Ekhator replacing Locatelli.

The squad remains stretched heading into the next round of European fixtures. McKennie is suffering from muscle fatigue and will miss the Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar. Alajbegovic and Cabal are expected to be available in the Netherlands. The trip comes with the European squad list already being reshaped.

#1567. Exor pays in €60m of Juventus’ €250m raise, but UEFA deal limits January plans

Juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it. Giovanni Carnevali warned that the UEFA settlement means nothing extraordinary should be expected in January.

Juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in new capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November. The vote came in the extraordinary part of the meeting and passed with 99.9% in favour. The same assembly approved the 2025/26 accounts.

Part of the money is already committed. Exor has already paid in €60m as an advance towards the capital increase. That payment supports the club’s equity and finances until the board uses its new authority. The majority owner has also guaranteed its own 65.4% stake in the raise and any shares other investors leave untaken.

The squad will not see the full sum. Shoring up the club’s finances across this season and next will take 45–50% of whatever is raised, according to Football Italia. That leaves roughly €100m mainly for first-team signings before the January window. Beyond keeping equity at a suitable level, the rest will go on controlling debt and keeping the team competitive, including transfers, Corriere dello Sport reports.

The accounts show why the balance sheet needs support. The consolidated loss for 2025/26 was €66.0m. That was €7.9m bigger than the previous year’s €58.1m. The result was in line with the forecasts in the club’s half-year report to 31 December 2025. The board had approved the accounts on 29 September. Another loss is expected in 2026/27, mainly because Juventus are in the Europa League rather than the Champions League.

The assembly was Giovanni Carnevali’s first as chief executive. He promised a serious approach to the January window. His warning was just as clear. As a serious company, Juventus must honour its settlement agreement with UEFA and does not expect to do anything extraordinary.

That agreement was announced on 30 June. It is a three-year settlement with the First Chamber of UEFA’s Club Financial Control Body. It relates to Juventus breaking UEFA’s Football Earnings Rule over the three seasons from 2022/23 to 2024/25.

For supporters, the message is mixed. The capital increase gives the club fresh resources. The settlement still dictates how quickly that money can be used on the pitch.

Shareholders also criticised the club for keeping a low profile in recent years. President Gianluca Ferrero declared Juventus open to dialogue with Tether.

The terms of the UEFA deal leave little margin. Missing the targets agreed with UEFA for the current season or the next two can lead to limits on the club’s UEFA List A and further sporting sanctions. The settlement runs until the 2027/28 financial year.
